t: Machinery breakdown and erection insurance were developed mainly by insurers in which country, where Munich Re played a pioneering role?
o: Germany
United Kingdom
Switzerland
Japan
e: While boiler insurance started in England, the machinery breakdown and erection all risks forms were developed in Germany in the early twentieth century.

t: Which engineering policy is annual and NOT linked to a construction or erection project?
o: Erection All Risks
Contractors' All Risks
Advance Loss of Profit
Electronic Equipment Insurance
e: EEI, MBD, BPP, CPM, DOS and CECR are annual operational covers; CAR, EAR and ALOP are project covers.

t: Which of the following would be covered under Section I of a CAR policy?
o: Cost of rectifying a wrongly set-out foundation discovered before concreting
Penalty for late completion imposed by the principal
Loss of a surveying instrument found missing at stock-taking
Collapse of a partly built retaining wall following heavy rain
e: Collapse due to rain is accidental physical damage; rectification of errors without damage, inventory losses and penalties are excluded.

t: Which of the following is excluded under Section II (TPL) of a CAR policy but can be bought back as an extension?
o: Liability arising from vibration, removal or weakening of support
Liability for injury to third parties on the site
Liability for damage to third-party property adjacent to the site
Legal costs incurred with the insurer's consent
e: Vibration/weakening of support is a standard TPL exclusion that can be added back with a sub-limit, usually after a pre-construction survey of neighbouring buildings.

t: A CAR policy of ₹100 crore sum insured is issued for a 30-month project. After 24 months the contractor requests a 6-month extension because of delays. The additional premium is normally charged:
o: Free of cost as the delay is not the contractor's fault
Only if a claim has not been lodged
At double the original rate
On a pro-rata basis for the extended period on the remaining value at risk, at the insurer's discretion
e: Extensions are granted at additional premium, normally pro-rata, with the underwriter free to review terms based on claims and remaining exposure.

t: A CAR policy for an apartment project has a sum insured of ₹45 crore, out of which ₹25 crore is contract value and ₹20 crore is free issue materials. The flat premium rate is 0.12% plus a terrorism rate of 0.03%. The total premium before GST is:
e: Premium is charged on the full sum insured of ₹45 crore at 0.15% (0.12% + 0.03%) = ₹6,75,000.

t: A third-party cross-liability extension under CAR Section II means that:
o: The principal and contractor are treated as separate insureds so that each can claim for injury or damage caused to the other as if a separate policy were issued
Liability is shared 50:50 between the parties
Each party pays half the premium
Third parties can claim directly against the insurer
e: Cross liability treats joint insureds as third parties to each other, subject to the overall limit of indemnity and excluding the works themselves.

t: Under an EAR policy, an unexplained loss discovered only on taking inventory is:
o: Covered in full
Covered if reported within 7 days
Covered subject to 25% excess
Excluded
e: Like CAR, EAR excludes inventory shortages because they cannot be linked to a sudden and unforeseen insured event.

t: Which of the following is an available extension to an EAR policy?
o: Dismantling of existing machinery at the site before erection of the new plant
Loss of the manufacturer's profit
Contractual penalties for delayed erection
Depreciation of the plant during storage
e: Dismantling of old plant, surrounding property, debris removal and extended maintenance are common add-ons; profit and penalties are excluded.

t: A client is erecting a 50 MW captive power plant valued at ₹300 crore, including ₹60 crore of civil works. The appropriate single engineering cover for the project is:
o: CAR for the whole project
MBD for the whole project
EAR for the whole project, with civil works included in the sum insured
CECR for the whole project
e: Where the mechanical/electrical plant is the dominant component, an EAR policy covering the civil portion as well is issued; CAR is for predominantly civil works.

t: An EAR policy is issued with a sum insured of ₹40 crore at a rate of 0.30% for the full project period. The premium before GST is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). ₹40,00,00,000 × 0.30% = ₹12,00,000; GST at 18% would be added on this amount.

t: Under an EAR policy, 'maintenance cover' normally means:
o: The insurer maintains the plant during the policy period
Cover for the plant during commercial operation
Cover for routine servicing costs
Cover for damage caused by the erection contractor while fulfilling maintenance obligations after commissioning
e: As under CAR, the maintenance (defects liability) period cover protects the erection contractor's exposure while attending to defects after handover.

t: An EAR policy excludes damage to the insured plant arising from:
o: Fall of a transformer while being lifted into position
Storm damage to crated equipment in open storage
Wear and tear, corrosion, oxidation and deterioration due to lack of use
Short circuit during cold testing
e: Gradual causes and deterioration are excluded under all engineering policies; sudden accidents during lifting, storage and testing are covered.

t: Which of the following items is NOT normally insured under a CPM policy?
o: Mobile crane
Hydraulic excavator
Batching plant
Dredger operating in a harbour
e: Waterborne vessels and craft are excluded from CPM and need marine hull cover; land-based plant is the subject matter.

t: A CPM policy is usually written for a period of:
o: 12 months, renewable annually
The duration of each project only
36 months
The life of the machine
e: CPM is an annual policy covering the contractor's fleet across sites, unlike CAR which follows the contract period.

t: A contractor's mobile crane insured under CPM for ₹1.5 crore (new replacement value) is damaged. Repair cost ₹20 lakh; the policy excess is 1% of sum insured. The amount payable is:
e: Excess = 1% of ₹1.5 crore = ₹1,50,000; payable = ₹20,00,000 − ₹1,50,000 = ₹18,50,000, repair cost being paid without depreciation.

t: Which of the following best describes the subject matter of MBD insurance?
o: Machinery while in transit to the factory
Machinery during erection and testing
Machinery in operation at the insured premises after successful commissioning, whether working, at rest or being overhauled
Machinery lying in the manufacturer's showroom
e: MBD is an operational cover; transit, erection and testing are marine and EAR subjects.

t: Under MBD, which of the following extensions can be purchased?
o: Cover for fire and lightning
Cover for inventory shortages
Loss due to wear and tear
Owner's surrounding property and third-party liability
e: Surrounding property, TPL, express freight, air freight, overtime and escalation are MBD add-ons; fire, wear and tear and inventory losses remain excluded.

t: A compressor insured under MBD for ₹8 lakh suffers a total loss. Its new replacement value at the time of loss is ₹10 lakh and depreciation works out to 30%. Ignoring excess and salvage, the insurer pays:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Total loss is settled at actual value (₹10 lakh less 30% = ₹7 lakh); as the sum insured is only 80% of the replacement value, average reduces this to ₹5,60,000.

t: Which of the following causes is covered under MBD?
o: Entry of a foreign body into a compressor cylinder
Flood water entering the machine room
Riot damage to a generator
Theft of a pump impeller
e: Foreign body entry, misalignment, vibration and centrifugal force are MBD perils; flood, riot and theft are fire/burglary perils.

t: The excess under an Indian MBD policy is normally expressed as:
o: A fixed amount of ₹10,000 for every claim
A percentage of the claim without any minimum
A percentage of the annual premium
A percentage of the sum insured of the affected item, subject to a minimum and maximum
e: MBD excesses are linked to the affected item's sum insured so that small claims on large machines are absorbed by the insured.

t: A transformer sum insured of ₹40 lakh under MBD is destroyed; replacement cost at the time of loss ₹50 lakh, depreciation 25%, salvage ₹2 lakh, excess 1% of sum insured. The claim payable is:
e: Actual value = ₹50 lakh − 25% = ₹37.5 lakh; average (40/50) gives ₹30 lakh; less salvage ₹2 lakh and excess ₹40,000 = ₹27,60,000.

t: A BPP policy is issued for:
o: Boilers and pressure plant during erection
Boilers and pressure plant in operation, against explosion and collapse in the ordinary course of working
Boilers in transit
Boilers while under hydraulic test
e: BPP is an operational annual cover; erection is under EAR and hydraulic tests are specifically excluded.

t: Which of the following is covered under the 'surrounding property' section of a BPP policy?
o: Damage to the insured's adjoining building caused by explosion of the boiler
Loss of production due to the explosion
Wear and tear of refractory lining
Damage to the boiler by a lightning strike
e: BPP covers damage to the insured's own property near the boiler caused by explosion or collapse; consequential loss and lightning are not BPP perils.

t: Which of the following is an exclusion under a BPP policy?
o: Explosion of an air receiver during normal working
Collapse of a steam drum due to crushing stress
Damage caused by overloading or experiments not sanctioned by the insurer
Third-party injury caused by explosion of a pressure vessel
e: Overloading, experiments and tests beyond normal working are excluded; the other items are core BPP perils.

t: Which of the following is a typical subject of an EEI policy?
o: Diesel generator set
Industrial boiler
Steam turbine
Hospital MRI scanner and computer installations
e: EEI is for electronic equipment such as computers, medical imaging, telecom and process control systems; rotating plant and boilers are MBD/BPP subjects.

t: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act, 1938 requires that:
o: No risk be assumed unless the premium is received in advance or guaranteed as prescribed
A licensed surveyor assess every engineering claim
All engineering risks be reinsured with GIC Re
Every policy be registered with IRDAI
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 64VB is the 'premium in advance' rule; it is why cover under CAR/EAR starts only after premium or instalment is received.

t: Under an EEI policy, cover for portable equipment such as laptops away from the insured premises is:
o: Automatically included anywhere in the world
Not available under any circumstances
Available as an extension, typically restricted to India
Included only if the equipment is less than one year old
e: The basic EEI cover applies at the specified premises; portable items can be extended for use anywhere within India at an additional premium.

t: A loss of data caused by a computer virus with no physical damage to the equipment is:
o: Covered under Section I of EEI
Covered under Section II of EEI
Excluded under the EEI policy
Covered under Section III of EEI
e: EEI Section II responds only to data loss following physical damage to the media; virus, programming errors and erroneous inputs are excluded.

t: An EEI policy carries an excess of 5% of the claim amount, minimum ₹2,500. A fire-fighting foam discharge damages a telephone exchange and the repair cost is ₹1,80,000. The amount payable is:
e: 5% of ₹1,80,000 = ₹9,000, which exceeds the minimum of ₹2,500; payable = ₹1,71,000.

t: Which of the following stocks is most commonly insured under DOS in India?
o: Cement in a godown
Garments in a showroom
Steel coils in a yard
Potatoes and other agricultural produce in cold storage
e: DOS is a cold storage cover for perishables such as potatoes, fruits, dairy and pharmaceuticals.

t: Under a DOS policy, the basis of indemnity is:
o: The replacement cost of the refrigeration plant
The value of the deteriorated stock (as insured) less salvage, subject to the sum insured and excess
The storage rent lost by the cold storage owner
The cost of electricity consumed during the period of breakdown
e: DOS pays for the deteriorated stock itself; neither plant repairs nor lost rent are covered.

t: Which of the following would be a valid DOS claim?
o: Stock spoiled because the cold storage was switched off to save electricity
Stock spoiled because it was already infected when brought in
Stock damaged by rodents in the chamber
Stock contaminated by accidental leakage of ammonia refrigerant into the chamber
e: Contamination by escape of refrigerant is an insured peril; deliberate switch-off, vermin and pre-existing infection are excluded.

t: Which of the following is excluded under a CECR policy?
o: Flood damage to a bridge pier
Landslide damaging a road embankment
Loss or damage due to faulty design or defective materials
Impact of a vessel against a jetty
e: Design and material defects are excluded, as under CAR; the other perils are named perils under CECR.

t: A State highway authority owns 400 km of completed roads and bridges. The most suitable cover is:
o: CAR policy with 12-month period
CECR policy, possibly on a first-loss basis for the AOG perils
CPM policy
EEI policy
e: CECR is designed for completed civil structures; large linear assets are often insured on a first-loss basis because a total loss is improbable.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: Which of the following must be declared by the principal while proposing for ALOP?
o: The contractor's bank guarantee
The site's distance from the nearest town
The list of sub-contractors' employees
The project schedule with the planned date of commencement of commercial operation and the basis of projected gross profit
e: ALOP underwriting hinges on the schedule and the profit projection, which fix the indemnity period and sum insured.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: Which of the following statements about ALOP is INCORRECT?
o: ALOP can be issued only together with a CAR/EAR material damage policy
ALOP covers delay caused by insured material damage during the construction phase
ALOP covers loss of profit arising from damage occurring during the maintenance period
ALOP indemnity begins after the time excess from the scheduled date of commencement
e: ALOP cover ends when the project is completed; delays caused by damage in the maintenance/defects period are not covered as the plant is already in operation.

t: IRDAI was constituted under the:
o: Insurance Act 1938
IRDA Act 1999
General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act 1972
LIC Act 1956
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The IRDA Act 1999 established the Authority; it began functioning in April 2000 and is headquartered in Hyderabad.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: Under MLOP, the 'indemnity period' is:
o: The policy period of 12 months
The period beginning with the breakdown during which business results are affected, not exceeding the period stated in the schedule
The period taken by the insurer to settle the claim
The period of warranty of the machine
e: The indemnity period limits the duration for which loss of gross profit is paid and is chosen with reference to the longest repair/replacement time.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: In an MLOP claim, the insured spends ₹8 lakh on hiring a stand-by generator, which avoids a loss of gross profit of ₹6 lakh. The amount admissible as increased cost of working is:
e: ICOW is admissible only up to the loss of gross profit it avoids (the economic limit), so ₹6 lakh is payable and ₹2 lakh is uneconomic expenditure.

topic: Advance Loss of Profits (ALOP) and Machinery Loss of Profits (MLOP)
t: The rate of premium for MLOP is normally related to:
o: The MBD rate on the machinery, the indemnity period and the time excess
The number of employees in the factory
The age of the factory building
The fire policy sum insured
e: MLOP rating follows the material damage rate adjusted for the length of the indemnity period and the size of the time excess.

t: A risk inspection before granting an MBD policy on a large plant is mainly intended to assess:
o: The colour scheme of the factory
The condition, age, maintenance practices and operating environment of the machinery and the availability of spares
The owner's credit rating
The location of the canteen
e: Physical condition and maintenance regimes are the key determinants of breakdown frequency and repair time.

t: In detariffed engineering business in India, the rates charged by insurers must be:
o: Identical to the erstwhile tariff rates
Based on the insurer's board-approved underwriting policy and filed/used in accordance with IRDAI product guidelines
Approved by the Tariff Advisory Committee for each policy
Fixed by GIC Re
e: After detariffing, insurers set their own rates subject to IRDAI's file-and-use/use-and-file framework and internal underwriting policy.

t: Which of the following is a typical rating factor for a CECR policy on a bridge?
o: Flood return period of the river and the bridge's age and construction
Number of vehicles owned by the authority
Distance from the nearest railway station
The number of toll booths
e: Hydrology, seismic zone and condition of the structure drive CECR rating.

t: Probable Maximum Loss (PML) assessment is used in engineering underwriting mainly to:
o: Fix the GST rate on the policy
Decide the retention and reinsurance requirement for a large project risk
Determine the excess on third-party claims
Calculate the depreciation on machinery
e: PML estimates the largest loss reasonably expected from a single event and guides retention, facultative placement and event limits for AOG perils.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital required to start a life or general insurance company in India is:
o: ₹50 crore
₹100 crore
₹200 crore
₹500 crore
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹100 crore for a direct insurer; ₹200 crore for a reinsurer (Section 6 of the Insurance Act).

t: Which of the following should an insured NOT do after a CAR loss?
o: Inform the insurer immediately
Take photographs and preserve evidence
Carry out full permanent repairs before the surveyor's inspection
Take emergency measures to prevent further damage
e: Permanent repairs before inspection prejudice the survey; emergency mitigation is required but full repairs need the insurer's consent or survey.

t: Under the 2024 IRDAI Protection of Policyholders' Interests regulations, after receiving the surveyor's report the insurer must decide the claim within:
o: 7 days
30 days
45 days
90 days
e: The 2024 regulations shortened the timelines: survey report within 15 days and claim decision within 7 days of the report (earlier 30 days).

t: In an engineering claim settlement, 'salvage' refers to:
o: The premium refund on cancellation
The residual value of damaged property which is deducted from the claim or taken over by the insurer
The cost of removing debris
The reinstated sum insured
e: Salvage value belongs to the insurer on payment of a total loss, or is deducted from the claim if retained by the insured.

t: Two policies — a CAR policy and a fire policy of the principal — both cover a damaged site office building. The principle governing the sharing of the loss between the insurers is:
o: Subrogation
Contribution
Utmost good faith
Proximate cause
e: Where two policies cover the same interest, subject matter and peril, the insurers share the loss rateably under the principle of contribution.
